subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Visual artworks about history and culture
altText: Basic 3 learners in Ghana studying pictures and artworks that show the history and culture of different Ghanaian communities.
detailedDescription: In a Basic 3 classroom, children sit in groups around tables covered with photos and simple reproductions of Ghanaian visual artworks such as historic buildings, chiefs, traditional symbols, and cultural scenes. They point and talk about what they see while the teacher guides them to notice history and culture reflected in the artworks. The scene shows learners using visual art to understand the story of different Ghanaian communities.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Visual artworks from other parts of Ghana
altText: Basic 3 pupils examining pictures of pots, carvings, baskets, cloth and signboards from different regions in Ghana.
detailedDescription: On a wall and table in a Basic 3 classroom, there are photos and simple sketches of visual artworks from different Ghanaian communities: clay pots, carved stools, woven baskets, printed cloth, leather sandals and hand-painted signboards. Learners stand and point at the artworks while the teacher prompts them to talk about materials, tools, and what each artwork is used for. The picture teaches learners to recognise the diversity of Ghanaian visual arts beyond their own locality.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Natural and manmade environments as inspiration
altText: Basic 3 learners sketching plants, buildings, roads and bridges from observation in their community.
detailedDescription: Basic 3 learners stand and sit around the school compound, sketching elements from the natural and manmade environment: trees, flowers, a small bridge, a roadside shop, and passing vehicles. Some pupils focus on shapes and lines, others on patterns and textures they can see. The teacher encourages them to look closely and think about how these everyday scenes can become subjects for meaningful artworks.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Topical issues as visual art themes
altText: Basic 3 children discussing pictures of flooding, poor waste disposal and road safety, planning artworks about these issues.
detailedDescription: Inside a Basic 3 classroom, learners sit in a circle around a set of pictures showing topical issues such as choked gutters, flooding, burning rubbish and unsafe road crossing. They discuss what is happening in each picture and how it affects people. The teacher asks how visual posters, drawings or murals could help change behaviour. The scene encourages learners to see art as a tool for addressing real community challenges.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Planning visual artworks from gathered ideas
altText: Basic 3 pupils using small sketches and notes to plan larger visual artworks on paper.
detailedDescription: In a classroom, Basic 3 pupils sit with sketchbooks and large sheets of paper. They choose ideas from previous observation drawings and notes, then make small planning sketches deciding what to include in a final artwork. Some pupils rough out compositions with light pencil lines, while the teacher encourages them to think about what story or message their picture will communicate.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 learners trying out crayons, paint, collage and simple printmaking on test sheets.
detailedDescription: On low tables, Basic 3 learners experiment with different visual art media: crayons, coloured pencils, watercolours, collage papers and simple printmaking using carved potatoes or foam. They test how each medium looks and feels, creating patches of colour, patterns and textures. The teacher encourages them to notice which media best fit the ideas they want to express in their final artworks.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 pupils working on larger drawings and paintings based on earlier sketches and research.
detailedDescription: At individual desks, Basic 3 learners develop larger artworks on cartridge paper or card. Next to each child is a small sketchbook with planning drawings and notes. The new artworks show more detail and clearer arrangements of people, buildings or environmental scenes. The teacher moves between tables, asking questions that help learners refine their ideas and improve their use of space, line and colour.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 learners arranging their sketches, colour tests and notes into a personal visual idea journal.
detailedDescription: Inside the classroom, Basic 3 pupils flip through small booklets that contain their observation sketches, colour tests and planning drawings. They sort and label pages, adding short phrases or symbols to remind them of future ideas. The teacher explains that these journals are like personal idea banks they can return to whenever they want to create new visual artworks.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Planning a simple visual arts exhibition
altText: Basic 3 pupils and their teacher planning how to arrange drawings and paintings on walls and tables for an exhibition.
detailedDescription: A Basic 3 class stands in front of a blank wall and a table. On another table are completed drawings and paintings. Some pupils hold artworks up to the wall to see where they might fit, while others look at a rough floor plan sketch. The teacher listens to their suggestions about grouping artworks by theme, topic or colour. The picture shows children learning to plan how their work will be shared with an audience.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 learners guiding classmates and a few parents around a classroom exhibition of artworks.
detailedDescription: The classroom has become a mini gallery with learners’ artworks neatly displayed on walls and tables. A Basic 3 pupil stands beside their piece explaining the meaning to classmates and one or two visiting adults. Another child leads a small group through the display, pointing out artworks about different topical issues. The teacher observes proudly as learners take ownership of presenting their creative work.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 pupils taking simple photos and making quick sketches of their classroom art exhibition for records.
detailedDescription: After the exhibition walk-through, some Basic 3 learners take simple photos of the displayed artworks using a tablet or phone held by the teacher, while others make small sketches of the overall arrangement in their notebooks. The teacher explains that documentation helps them remember what they created and how they displayed it, building a record of their growth as artists.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 pupils sitting in a circle giving kind and specific feedback on each other’s drawings and paintings.
detailedDescription: Basic 3 learners sit in a circle with a selection of artworks placed where everyone can see. One pupil holds a simple feedback card and comments on what they like about a classmate’s work, while another suggests one thing that could be improved. The teacher writes some of the feedback sentences on a chart titled ‘What we did well’ and ‘Next time we will…’. The scene teaches respectful, constructive critique.

subject: Basic 3 Creative Arts
altText: Basic 3 learners quietly writing or drawing simple reflections about their own artworks.
detailedDescription: Individual Basic 3 pupils sit at their desks with their own artwork in front of them and a small reflection sheet. They answer prompts like ‘I am proud of…’, ‘This was difficult because…’, and ‘Next time I will…’. Some children draw small symbols or faces to show their feelings. The teacher walks around gently encouraging honest self-assessment and helping learners set personal goals for improvement.
